# Overview > Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat entry point) ## Mission Help a BMW product manager derive, justify, and prioritize customer-facing requirements for the successor of an existing vehicle line — grounded in customer feedback, BMW product/sales data, and web research — while the PM stays in control of every decision that matters. ## Scope **In scope:** customer-facing product requirements — features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging *as experienced by the customer*, variant and package offering. **Out of scope:** regulatory/homologation (safety, emissions, type approval), engineering specs/architecture/supplier topics, pricing/business-case/cost calculation (cost or effort may be used as a *rough* prioritization factor only). A finding that reads as regulatory or pricing in nature is auto-tagged and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of scope" bin rather than drafted into a requirement — see [`08-scaling-and-config.md`](08-scaling-and-config.md#regulatory-guardrail). ## Demonstration scope - **Vehicle lines in the provided data:** F70, G60, G70 (presumed 1 / 5 / 7 Series successors — confirm before presenting as fact) - **Markets:** Europe, China, United States, or a subset - **Demo pick:** G60 (5 Series) × Europe, full vertical slice; other lines/markets loaded and runnable on request to prove it isn't a one-off ## The five stages Taken directly from BMW's own process slide — everything in this doc set is organized around it. ```mermaid flowchart LR SA["01 Situation analysis
baseline · competition ·
feedback · trends"] SC["02 Structure & context
classify · cluster ·
dedupe · contextualize"] RD["03 Requirements definition
specify · quantify ·
acceptance criteria"] PR["04 Prioritization
customer vs business,
explainable score"] DOC["05 Documentation
dossier · audit trail ·
re-embed into KB"] SA --> SC --> RD --> PR --> DOC DOC -.->|requirements tracking loop,
~quarterly over ~2 yrs| SA ``` What makes this more than a batch pipeline is **how** a PM drives it — see [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md): the PM starts a **chat** with a research request, an **orchestrator** plans which agents are needed, and they run one at a time. Each agent's cited answer can be pushed back on or accepted before the next agent starts, and the final result appears only after all needed agents are accepted. Not every request runs every stage. See [decision 0005](../decisions/0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md). ## Document map See [`../README.md`](../README.md) for the full doc index. Start with [`01-agents.md`](01-agents.md) for who does what, then [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) for how a PM actually drives this. # Agents > Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (orchestrator plans agents) Every agent reads some slice of evidence and produces either new evidence (`Finding`s) or a synthesis of existing evidence (`Cluster`, `Requirement`, `Score`, dossier). None of them change a requirement's status, priority tier, or scope on their own — see [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) for how their output actually gets used. ## Roster | Agent | Stage | Reads | Produces | |---|---|---|---| | Baseline Agent | 01 Situation analysis | Previous-gen feedback, BMW portfolio docs, prior sales trend | Findings tagged `strategic_continuity` | | Customer Feedback Agent | 01 | `*_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`, `*_customer_studies.xlsx` | Findings (`complaint` / `unmet_need` / `praise`), each with sample size + market | | Sales & Portfolio Agent | 01 | `sales_volumes.xlsx`, parsed OptionList rows | Revealed-preference findings — option uptake % as a `business_signal` input | | Competitor Agent | 01 | Live web search — competitor spec pages, reviews, teardown data | Findings tagged `competitor_advantage`, source-trust tier | | Market & Trend Agent | 01 | Live web search — trend reports, forward-looking analyst pieces | Findings tagged `market_trend`; explicitly flagged as assumption-heavy, not fact | | Clustering / Ontology Agent | 02 | All findings across sources | Deduplicated clusters mapped onto the domain taxonomy | | Critic Agent | cross-cutting | Any agent's draft output before it reaches the PM | Verifies every claim has a live citation; flags unsupported or weakly-sourced statements and forces a retry before the step reaches `awaiting_review` | | Requirements Drafting Agent (Synthesizer) | 03 | Clusters + linked findings | Draft requirement: description, metric, acceptance criteria | | Prioritization Agent | 04 | Draft requirements + findings + sales/option data | Score + weight breakdown + one-line rationale | | Documentation Agent | 05 | Every accepted step + every PM decision in a run | Human-readable dossier (markdown), re-embedded into the knowledge layer | | Delta / Tracking Agent | ongoing | New ingestion batches vs. existing requirement evidence | `new evidence` / `contradicting` / `stale` flags, routed to PM review | Competitor and Market/Trend are kept as **two separate agents**, not one: competitor findings are closer to verifiable fact (a rival ships a feature or doesn't), while trend findings are inherently speculative (what will 2030 customers want). Collapsing them into one "market research" agent was the original shape of this design — splitting them keeps that evidence-character difference visible in each requirement's assumptions. See [`decisions/0003-critic-agent-and-agent-split.md`](../decisions/0003-critic-agent-and-agent-split.md). How the Competitor Agent decides *which* rivals to look at and makes their evidence comparable is its own doc: [`10-competitor-benchmarking.md`](10-competitor-benchmarking.md). ## The Critic Agent The Critic doesn't sit at a stage of its own — it sits between every agent and the PM. Before any step reaches `awaiting_review`, the Critic Agent: 1. Checks that every factual claim in the agent's output links to a real source with a locator (page/row for provided files, URL + retrieval date for web sources). 2. Flags claims that don't — the step is automatically sent back for a retry (same agent, same scope, instructed to either find a citation or drop the claim) *before* the PM ever sees it. 3. Downgrades `evidence_level` on anything that's technically cited but thin (single source, no corroboration, low source-trust tier) rather than silently passing it through at full confidence. This is what makes "push back on agent results" cheap for the PM: obviously weak output never reaches the review queue in the first place. The PM still pushes back on anything the Critic let through but the PM disagrees with — that's a normal `Retry` or `Reject` action on the step, see next doc. ## Orchestrator Not an agent that produces findings. It does three things: 1. **Plans.** Reads the PM's chat request and chooses which agents are needed, with a one-line reason each. The plan is shown in the chat and the PM can edit it. 2. **Sequences.** Holds the `PipelineRun`/`Step` state machine (see next doc) and starts the next planned agent when the PM accepts the current one, passing along the accepted output as context. 3. **Adapts.** May propose adding or dropping agents as results come in; the PM can veto, and a step already accepted is never silently re-run. Not every request uses every agent. See [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) and [decision 0005](../decisions/0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md). # Tech stack > Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (Supabase + OpenAI embeddings, see decision 0004) Kept boring on purpose — a hackathon is not the place to debug infrastructure. | Layer | Choice | Why | |---|---|---| | Orchestration | LangGraph | Its explicit interrupt-for-human-input pattern maps directly onto the per-step PM gates in [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) — one `interrupt()` per `Step`, not one at the end, plus a planner node where the orchestrator chooses the agents. Its Postgres checkpointer stores run state in the same Supabase database (use the direct or session-pooler connection string, not the transaction pooler) | | LLM | Claude | Extraction, cluster labeling, requirement drafting, scoring rationale, Critic verification | | Web research | Search API tool-call (Tavily/Brave) | Source-trust tagging applied at ingest time, not after the fact | | PDF parsing | `pdftotext -layout` (poppler) for text; pdfplumber / vision-LLM still planned for the equipment tables | Text extraction works (the catalogs have real text). Reliable ■/□ column mapping needs table-aware extraction or a vision pass — not built yet | | Excel | openpyxl (+ psycopg for loading) | Loaders in `ingest/`; the customer-study cross-tabs need a custom parser | | Storage | Supabase (managed Postgres) + pgvector 0.8 | One database for both relational entities (`Finding`, `Requirement`, `AuditEvent`, …) and embeddings — keeps traceability joins simple instead of reconciling two stores. Schema is live: see `supabase/migrations/`. RLS is on for every table with no policies yet, so only the backend (service role / direct connection) can read or write; the frontend goes through the API | | Embeddings | OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dims, cosine, HNSW) | Key in `.env` as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Only `finding.text` and `chunk.content` are embedded; option codes and sales numbers stay exact, un-embedded data. Changing the model means re-embedding and altering the column — see [decision 0004](../decisions/0004-supabase-and-openai-embeddings.md) | | API | FastAPI | — | | Frontend | React + shadcn/ui | Chat thread with step cards (Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject) and a plan strip, evidence panel with citations, score breakdown, audit timeline | | Deploy | Docker-compose / Vercel demo instance; Supabase hosts the database and raw-file storage | Single environment for the demo |

# Analysis & structuring

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10

Stages 01 (situation analysis) and 02 (structure & context) of the pipeline: from raw findings to
deduplicated themes. Derived from [`01-agents.md`](../architecture/01-agents.md),
[`10-competitor-benchmarking.md`](../architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md) and
[`08-scaling-and-config.md`](../architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md).

## Situation analysis

| ID | Requirement | Prio | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-AN-01 | Derive a baseline from the previous generation — what customers valued and criticised, how sales developed — as findings marked as strategic continuity. | S | [01](../architecture/01-agents.md#roster) |
| FR-AN-02 | Extract complaints, unmet needs and praise from customer feedback, each with its market and, where the source provides one, its sample size. | M | [01](../architecture/01-agents.md#roster) |
| FR-AN-03 | Compute option uptake per market from sales volumes and the option list, as a revealed-preference signal alongside what customers say. | M | [01](../architecture/01-agents.md#roster) |
| FR-AN-04 | Identify market and technology trends from web research, and label every such finding as an assumption about the future rather than an observed fact. | S | [01](../architecture/01-agents.md#roster), [ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-critic-agent-and-agent-split.md) |
| FR-AN-05 | Classify every finding by signal type and sentiment. | M | [04](../architecture/04-data-model.md#finding) |

## Competitor benchmarking

| ID | Requirement | Prio | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-AN-06 | Let the PM fix an anchor vehicle (line and variant) and propose a segment — price, body style, seats, powertrain, range, size — that the PM can override band by band before any search runs. | S | [10](../architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md#2--segment-definition-what-the-same-bracket-means) |
| FR-AN-07 | List the rival models inside the segment per market, ranked by similarity, and let the PM choose which to carry forward. | S | [10](../architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md#4--shortlist-pick-the-comparison-vehicles) |
| FR-AN-08 | Compare anchor and rivals per aspect and per source type — owner voice with owner voice, test with test, spec with spec — in relative terms, and report "insufficient data" where either side is thin. | S | [10](../architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md#6--relative-comparison-against-the-anchor) |
| FR-AN-09 | Compare specifications only where both sides use the same measurement standard. | S | [10](../architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md#6--relative-comparison-against-the-anchor) |
| FR-AN-10 | Turn clear deltas into findings: a competitor advantage where the rival leads, a strength to defend where BMW leads. | M | [10](../architecture/10-competitor-benchmarking.md#6--relative-comparison-against-the-anchor) |

For the demo, `FR-AN-10` is satisfied with a hand-confirmed rival set; `FR-AN-06` to `FR-AN-09`
describe the full path and remain a proposal until the architecture adopts it.

## Structure & context

| ID | Requirement | Prio | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-AN-11 | Group findings that describe the same customer issue into one cluster, across sources and input families, and show which findings each cluster contains. | M | [01](../architecture/01-agents.md#roster) |
| FR-AN-12 | Map every cluster onto the domain taxonomy (Exterior, Interior, Powertrain, Driver Assistance, Infotainment, Comfort & Space, Usability, Variant & Package). | M | [08](../architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md#domain-taxonomy-is-config-not-code) |
| FR-AN-13 | Let the PM merge, split and relabel clusters and move a finding between clusters. | M | [02](../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md#the-four-actions-same-verbs-as-everywhere-else) |
| FR-AN-14 | Detect findings that are regulatory, engineering-internal or pricing in nature and route them to a visible out-of-scope bin instead of into a cluster. | M | [08](../architecture/08-scaling-and-config.md#regulatory-guardrail) |

**FR-AN-11** — a cluster reports how many independent sources and how many input families it draws
on. Twenty forum posts quoting one article count as one independent source.
# Requirements & prioritization

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10

Stages 03 (requirements definition) and 04 (prioritization). Derived from
[`04-data-model.md`](../architecture/04-data-model.md#requirement) and
[`06-prioritization.md`](../architecture/06-prioritization.md).

## Requirements definition

| ID | Requirement | Prio | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-RQ-01 | Draft a requirement from a cluster: title, description from the customer's point of view, domain, markets, vehicle line. | M | [01](../architecture/01-agents.md#roster) |
| FR-RQ-02 | Give every requirement a measurable metric and acceptance criteria; where no defensible number exists, say so explicitly instead of inventing one. | M | [04](../architecture/04-data-model.md#requirement) |
| FR-RQ-03 | Link every requirement to the findings and clusters it rests on. | M | [04](../architecture/04-data-model.md#requirement) |
| FR-RQ-04 | List the assumptions and uncertainties behind each requirement separately from its evidence. | M | [04](../architecture/04-data-model.md#requirement) |
| FR-RQ-05 | Show an overall evidence level per requirement, derived from its linked findings. | M | [04](../architecture/04-data-model.md#requirement) |
| FR-RQ-06 | Let the PM edit any field of a requirement; every edit is recorded with its reason. | M | [07](../architecture/07-audit-trail.md) |
| FR-RQ-07 | Flag requirements that overlap with or contradict an existing one before the PM approves a duplicate. | S | new |
| FR-RQ-08 | Let the PM create a requirement by hand and attach existing findings to it, marked as PM-originated. | C | new |

## Prioritization

| ID | Requirement | Prio | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-PR-01 | Score every requirement as a composite of customer relevance, business signal, strategic fit and effort, and show each component's value and weight. | M | [06](../architecture/06-prioritization.md) |
| FR-PR-02 | Base customer relevance on prevalence relative to sample size, sentiment severity and the number of independent corroborating sources — not on raw mention counts or social reach. | M | [06](../architecture/06-prioritization.md), `FR-IN-13` |
| FR-PR-03 | Show confidence as its own indicator, separate from the rank. | M | [06](../architecture/06-prioritization.md) |
| FR-PR-04 | Assign a tier — must-have, should-have, watch-list — from the composite score. | M | [06](../architecture/06-prioritization.md#worked-example) |
| FR-PR-05 | Let the PM change the weights per program and override any single component, then re-score. | M | [06](../architecture/06-prioritization.md) |
| FR-PR-06 | Keep every earlier score with the weights it used; re-scoring adds a version, it never overwrites. | M | [04](../architecture/04-data-model.md#score) |
| FR-PR-07 | Generate a one-sentence rationale per score that names the evidence driving it. | M | [06](../architecture/06-prioritization.md) |

**FR-PR-03** — "high potential, thin evidence" and "confidently low priority" must look different
in every list and export, not only on the detail page.

**FR-PR-04** — tier thresholds (currently ≥ 0.65 / 0.40–0.65 / < 0.40) are configuration. A PM
override of a tier is allowed, is recorded with a reason, and stays visibly marked as an override.
# PM overview

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10

The architecture specifies how a PM drives one run
([`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md#ui-shape)).
It does not yet specify where a PM looks to answer the questions asked in every program review:
*What do we have? How sure are we? What needs me? What changed?* This doc does. Almost all of it is
`new`; it adds views over data the architecture already stores, and needs no new entities.

## The four questions

# Requirement lifecycle & the two-year tracking loop

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

This is the *long-horizon* state of a requirement once it has made it out of a
[run](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) — weeks to months, across the life of the
~two-year requirements program, not the minutes-scale step-by-step approval inside a single run.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> PM_Review: PM reviews
    PM_Review --> Tracked: approve
    PM_Review --> Rejected: reject
    PM_Review --> Challenged: challenge / request evidence
    Challenged --> Draft: agent re-research
    Tracked --> Delta_Check: scheduled re-ingestion
    Delta_Check --> Tracked: no material change
    Delta_Check --> PM_Review: new / contradicting evidence
    Tracked --> Superseded: PM supersedes
    Rejected --> [*]
    Superseded --> [*]
```

- **`Draft` and `Delta_Check` run unattended.** Every other transition needs a PM action and a
  recorded reason — same four verbs as everywhere else in this system: approve, reject, edit
  (not shown as a separate state — it mutates `Draft` in place), challenge.
- **"No material change" stays quiet.** The Delta Agent re-checks tracked requirements against
  freshly ingested evidence on a recurring schedule (~quarterly) and only re-opens `PM_Review` when
  something actually moved — new corroboration, a contradiction, or evidence old enough to flag as
  stale. It never updates a tracked requirement's status on its own.
- **This is the "requirements tracking" loop** from BMW's own process slide, and the mechanism
  behind "the requirement process isn't performed once — it's a process over ~2 years."

## Relationship to the per-run approval chain

A requirement enters this state machine at `Draft` the moment a
[`PipelineRun`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md#data-model-additions)'s Documentation
step is accepted. Everything before that — the orchestrator's plan, reviewing each agent's
human-readable output in the chat, retrying or rejecting a step — happens *inside* the run, at a finer grain than this
diagram shows. Think of this doc as "what happens after the research is done and a requirement
exists," and [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md)
as "how the research itself gets approved."

## Committee / board mode

For the "large committee discusses this" pattern: several `Tracked`-or-`PM_Review` requirements
can be bundled into a generated board pack (a set of Documentation Agent dossiers). The
committee's collective call is still recorded as **one** audit event, with participants and
rationale noted, against one accountable PM — diffusing the discussion is fine, diffusing
accountability for the recorded decision is not.
# Prioritization

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10

A composite score the PM can see decomposed, re-weight, and override — never a black-box rank. It
balances what BMW's own slide calls "Customer" against "Business," plus the brief's allowance for
a rough cost/effort factor.

```
score = w_c · customer_relevance + w_b · business_signal + w_s · strategic_fit − w_e · effort_proxy
```

Default weights (PM-editable per program): `w_c = 0.40`, `w_b = 0.25`, `w_s = 0.15`, `w_e = 0.20`.
Not tuned to any real dataset — a defensible starting point, nothing more.

| Component | Derived from |
|---|---|
| `customer_relevance` | Finding prevalence normalized by sample size, sentiment severity, cross-source corroboration count, market-weighted when several markets are in scope |
| `business_signal` | Uptake % of the related option in `sales_volumes.xlsx`, plus competitor-coverage gap from the Competitor Agent. A sellability proxy, not a cost model — pricing/business-case math is out of scope |
| `strategic_fit` | Continuity with the previous-generation baseline (Baseline Agent) and the PM's stated themes for this program |
| `effort_proxy` | Coarse Low/Med/High heuristic (new hardware > software/UX change). Deliberately rough, always PM-editable |
| `confidence` | Evidence-level mix + source independence count. Shown as a **separate badge**, never folded silently into rank, so "high potential, thin evidence" stays visually distinct from "confidently low priority" |

Every stored `Score` keeps the weight vector used, each raw component value, who/what computed it,
a timestamp, and a one-line generated rationale — see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#score) — and is versioned, so re-scoring after new evidence
never erases what a priority call used to look like.

## Worked example

`R-2031` — *Fast-response seat ventilation*, built around BMW's own slide example.

- **Score:** 0.49 / 1.00 → Tier 2 (should-have). Tiers: ≥0.65 must-have, 0.40–0.65 should-have,
  <0.40 watch-list.
- **customer_relevance 0.78** — two independent BMW-internal findings (a verbatim complaint and a
  customer-study item scored 2.9/5, n=340, EU) corroborate a comfort gap.
- **business_signal 0.41** — moderate option-uptake signal; one competitor review notes a faster
  rival response time (review-estimated, not lab-verified — flagged as an assumption).
- **strategic_fit 0.60** — aligns with the program's stated comfort-parity theme.
- **effort_proxy low** — software/calibration change, not new hardware.
- **confidence 0.65** — moderate; EU-only sample so far, no lab-verified benchmark yet.

Rationale (agent-generated): *"Two independent BMW-internal sources plus one competitor review
corroborate a comfort gap; moderate business signal from option uptake; low estimated effort —
lands mid-tier pending a lab-verified response-time benchmark."*

Full linked findings, assumptions, and its audit trail are in
[`07-audit-trail.md`](07-audit-trail.md#worked-example-r-2031).
# Audit trail

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (plan events)

One append-only `AuditEvent` log underlies everything: every orchestrator plan and plan change, every `Step` start/accept/edit/retry/reject
inside a run (a step "starts" automatically when the previous one is accepted, so the start event
records which acceptance triggered it), and every requirement-level approve/edit/reject/challenge afterward. Nothing updates
a record in place without also writing one of these.

## Schema

`id, entity_type, entity_id, actor, action, before, after, rationale, timestamp`

- `actor` — an agent name (`PrioritizationAgent`) or a PM identity. Never ambiguous about who/what.
- `rationale` — required for every PM-initiated action. The UI will not commit a status change
  without it (see [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md)).
- `before` / `after` — enough of the record's state to render a diff, not the whole object.

## Worked example: R-2031

The full requirement (linked findings, assumptions, score breakdown) is in
[`06-prioritization.md`](06-prioritization.md#worked-example). Its audit trail:

| Timestamp | Actor | Action | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-14 09:02 | RequirementsDraftingAgent | Created R-2031 — `draft` | "3 corroborating findings clustered under Interior/Comfort::Seat Ventilation" |
| 2026-01-14 09:03 | PrioritizationAgent | Scored R-2031 — composite 0.49, Tier 2, weights v1.3 | — |
| 2026-01-16 14:51 | PM | Edited acceptance criteria: 140s → 75s | "Align with fleet thermal-comfort benchmark, not a customer time-guess" |
| 2026-01-16 14:52 | PM | Approved — `draft` → `tracked` | — |
| 2026-04-02 03:10 | DeltaAgent | Flagged new finding F-517 (competitor launch review) | "New evidence available, re-review suggested" |
| 2026-04-03 10:20 | PM | Reviewed, kept `tracked` | "New evidence reinforces the existing decision, no scope change" |

Every field the brief's audit-trail deliverable asks for falls out of this table directly: who or
what initiated each change, when, and the documented rationale — queryable, not a screenshot of a
decision.
# Scaling & configuration

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

Nothing about G60 or "Europe" is hardcoded. Every `PipelineRun` (one per chat request) takes a config:
`{vehicle_line, market, generation_baseline}`, read from the PM's message or asked back by the
orchestrator if missing. Swapping to the 1 Series in China is a config
change, not a rewrite.

## Domain taxonomy is config, not code

Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver Assistance / Infotainment / Comfort & Space / Usability
/ Variant & Package — stored as an editable `Ontology` store (see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#ontology)), not a hardcoded enum, so a future BEV-only line
can extend it without a code change.

## New source = one adapter

Every ingestion agent implements the same `Source → Finding[]` interface (see
[`03-ingestion.md`](03-ingestion.md)). A new feedback export, a new web source, a new internal
system plugs in without touching clustering, drafting, or scoring.

## Markets compose, they don't collapse

A requirement can carry per-market sub-scores and a market-fit flag ("fits EU, doesn't fit China")
rather than forcing one global priority — this is the direct answer to the PM pain point raised
about balancing requirements across regions with different climate, usage, and culture.

## Regulatory guardrail

Findings that read as safety/emissions/type-approval or pricing/business-case in nature are
auto-tagged by the Clustering/Ontology Agent and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of
scope" bin — never drafted into a customer requirement. Keeps the demo honestly inside the brief's
boundary instead of silently drifting into engineering or regulatory territory.

back to the exact cell or paragraph that produced it; a PM looking at the audit log can tell who or

`id, type (internal_pdf | internal_xlsx | web), uri, vehicle_line, market, retrieved_at`

`id, source_id, locator (page/row/cell or url+retrieved_at), text, signal_type (complaint |
unmet_need | competitor_advantage | market_trend | praise), evidence_level (Verified | Interpreted
| source-trust tier), sentiment, sample_size, market, extracted_by, created_at`

`id, kind (domain | market | vehicle_line), key, label, parent_id (nullable), active`

(Exterior/Interior/Powertrain/…) and the vehicle-line/market lists config, not code.

acceptance_criteria, evidence_level, assumptions[], uncertainties[], status (draft | pm_review |
tracked | rejected | challenged | superseded | proposed), linked_finding_ids[],
linked_cluster_ids[], origin (scheduled_pipeline | pm_query), created_by_run_id`

# Requirement lifecycle & the two-year tracking loop

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

This is the *long-horizon* state of a requirement once it has made it out of a
[run](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) — weeks to months, across the life of the
~two-year requirements program, not the minutes-scale step-by-step approval inside a single run.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> PM_Review: PM reviews
    PM_Review --> Tracked: approve
    PM_Review --> Rejected: reject
    PM_Review --> Challenged: challenge / request evidence
    Challenged --> Draft: agent re-research
    Tracked --> Delta_Check: scheduled re-ingestion
    Delta_Check --> Tracked: no material change
    Delta_Check --> PM_Review: new / contradicting evidence
    Tracked --> Superseded: PM supersedes
    Rejected --> [*]
    Superseded --> [*]
```

- **`Draft` and `Delta_Check` run unattended.** Every other transition needs a PM action and a
  recorded reason — same four verbs as everywhere else in this system: approve, reject, edit
  (not shown as a separate state — it mutates `Draft` in place), challenge.
- **"No material change" stays quiet.** The Delta Agent re-checks tracked requirements against
  freshly ingested evidence on a recurring schedule (~quarterly) and only re-opens `PM_Review` when
  something actually moved — new corroboration, a contradiction, or evidence old enough to flag as
  stale. It never updates a tracked requirement's status on its own.
- **This is the "requirements tracking" loop** from BMW's own process slide, and the mechanism
  behind "the requirement process isn't performed once — it's a process over ~2 years."

## Relationship to the per-run approval chain

A requirement enters this state machine at `Draft` the moment a
[`PipelineRun`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md#data-model-additions)'s Documentation
step is accepted. Everything before that — the orchestrator's plan, reviewing each agent's
human-readable output in the chat, retrying or rejecting a step — happens *inside* the run, at a finer grain than this
diagram shows. Think of this doc as "what happens after the research is done and a requirement
exists," and [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md)
as "how the research itself gets approved."

## Committee / board mode

For the "large committee discusses this" pattern: several `Tracked`-or-`PM_Review` requirements
can be bundled into a generated board pack (a set of Documentation Agent dossiers). The
committee's collective call is still recorded as **one** audit event, with participants and
rationale noted, against one accountable PM — diffusing the discussion is fine, diffusing
accountability for the recorded decision is not.
# Prioritization

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10

A composite score the PM can see decomposed, re-weight, and override — never a black-box rank. It
balances what BMW's own slide calls "Customer" against "Business," plus the brief's allowance for
a rough cost/effort factor.

```
score = w_c · customer_relevance + w_b · business_signal + w_s · strategic_fit − w_e · effort_proxy
```

Default weights (PM-editable per program): `w_c = 0.40`, `w_b = 0.25`, `w_s = 0.15`, `w_e = 0.20`.
Not tuned to any real dataset — a defensible starting point, nothing more.

| Component | Derived from |
|---|---|
| `customer_relevance` | Finding prevalence normalized by sample size, sentiment severity, cross-source corroboration count, market-weighted when several markets are in scope |
| `business_signal` | Uptake % of the related option in `sales_volumes.xlsx`, plus competitor-coverage gap from the Competitor Agent. A sellability proxy, not a cost model — pricing/business-case math is out of scope |
| `strategic_fit` | Continuity with the previous-generation baseline (Baseline Agent) and the PM's stated themes for this program |
| `effort_proxy` | Coarse Low/Med/High heuristic (new hardware > software/UX change). Deliberately rough, always PM-editable |
| `confidence` | Evidence-level mix + source independence count. Shown as a **separate badge**, never folded silently into rank, so "high potential, thin evidence" stays visually distinct from "confidently low priority" |

Every stored `Score` keeps the weight vector used, each raw component value, who/what computed it,
a timestamp, and a one-line generated rationale — see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#score) — and is versioned, so re-scoring after new evidence
never erases what a priority call used to look like.

## Worked example

`R-2031` — *Fast-response seat ventilation*, built around BMW's own slide example.

- **Score:** 0.49 / 1.00 → Tier 2 (should-have). Tiers: ≥0.65 must-have, 0.40–0.65 should-have,
  <0.40 watch-list.
- **customer_relevance 0.78** — two independent BMW-internal findings (a verbatim complaint and a
  customer-study item scored 2.9/5, n=340, EU) corroborate a comfort gap.
- **business_signal 0.41** — moderate option-uptake signal; one competitor review notes a faster
  rival response time (review-estimated, not lab-verified — flagged as an assumption).
- **strategic_fit 0.60** — aligns with the program's stated comfort-parity theme.
- **effort_proxy low** — software/calibration change, not new hardware.
- **confidence 0.65** — moderate; EU-only sample so far, no lab-verified benchmark yet.

Rationale (agent-generated): *"Two independent BMW-internal sources plus one competitor review
corroborate a comfort gap; moderate business signal from option uptake; low estimated effort —
lands mid-tier pending a lab-verified response-time benchmark."*

Full linked findings, assumptions, and its audit trail are in
[`07-audit-trail.md`](07-audit-trail.md#worked-example-r-2031).
# Audit trail

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (plan events)

One append-only `AuditEvent` log underlies everything: every orchestrator plan and plan change, every `Step` start/accept/edit/retry/reject
inside a run (a step "starts" automatically when the previous one is accepted, so the start event
records which acceptance triggered it), and every requirement-level approve/edit/reject/challenge afterward. Nothing updates
a record in place without also writing one of these.

## Schema

`id, entity_type, entity_id, actor, action, before, after, rationale, timestamp`

- `actor` — an agent name (`PrioritizationAgent`) or a PM identity. Never ambiguous about who/what.
- `rationale` — required for every PM-initiated action. The UI will not commit a status change
  without it (see [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md)).
- `before` / `after` — enough of the record's state to render a diff, not the whole object.

## Worked example: R-2031

The full requirement (linked findings, assumptions, score breakdown) is in
[`06-prioritization.md`](06-prioritization.md#worked-example). Its audit trail:

| Timestamp | Actor | Action | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-14 09:02 | RequirementsDraftingAgent | Created R-2031 — `draft` | "3 corroborating findings clustered under Interior/Comfort::Seat Ventilation" |
| 2026-01-14 09:03 | PrioritizationAgent | Scored R-2031 — composite 0.49, Tier 2, weights v1.3 | — |
| 2026-01-16 14:51 | PM | Edited acceptance criteria: 140s → 75s | "Align with fleet thermal-comfort benchmark, not a customer time-guess" |
| 2026-01-16 14:52 | PM | Approved — `draft` → `tracked` | — |
| 2026-04-02 03:10 | DeltaAgent | Flagged new finding F-517 (competitor launch review) | "New evidence available, re-review suggested" |
| 2026-04-03 10:20 | PM | Reviewed, kept `tracked` | "New evidence reinforces the existing decision, no scope change" |

Every field the brief's audit-trail deliverable asks for falls out of this table directly: who or
what initiated each change, when, and the documented rationale — queryable, not a screenshot of a
decision.
# Scaling & configuration

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

Nothing about G60 or "Europe" is hardcoded. Every `PipelineRun` (one per chat request) takes a config:
`{vehicle_line, market, generation_baseline}`, read from the PM's message or asked back by the
orchestrator if missing. Swapping to the 1 Series in China is a config
change, not a rewrite.

## Domain taxonomy is config, not code

Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver Assistance / Infotainment / Comfort & Space / Usability
/ Variant & Package — stored as an editable `Ontology` store (see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#ontology)), not a hardcoded enum, so a future BEV-only line
can extend it without a code change.

## New source = one adapter

Every ingestion agent implements the same `Source → Finding[]` interface (see
[`03-ingestion.md`](03-ingestion.md)). A new feedback export, a new web source, a new internal
system plugs in without touching clustering, drafting, or scoring.

## Markets compose, they don't collapse

A requirement can carry per-market sub-scores and a market-fit flag ("fits EU, doesn't fit China")
rather than forcing one global priority — this is the direct answer to the PM pain point raised
about balancing requirements across regions with different climate, usage, and culture.

## Regulatory guardrail

Findings that read as safety/emissions/type-approval or pricing/business-case in nature are
auto-tagged by the Clustering/Ontology Agent and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of
scope" bin — never drafted into a customer requirement. Keeps the demo honestly inside the brief's
boundary instead of silently drifting into engineering or regulatory territory.

# 0001 — Two-tier PDF ingestion instead of naive text extraction

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

The provided PDFs (`*_OptionList.PDF`) are structured option/equipment listings. The brief asks
for findings and requirements that are traceable to their sources. A naive "dump the PDF to text,
chunk by token count, embed" pipeline would destroy the table structure and produce citations like
"chunk 47" instead of a page/row a PM could actually go look at.

## Decision

Parse every PDF (and, by extension, every source) on two tracks:

1. **Deterministic** — layout-aware table extraction into typed rows, no model in the loop. Feeds
   structured stores (e.g. an `Options` table) directly.
2. **Semantic** — heading-aware chunking + embedding for narrative text, locator kept per chunk.

Both converge on a `Finding` with a locator and an `evidence_level` set by *how* it was extracted
(`Verified` for deterministic, `Interpreted` for semantic — further gradable by the Critic Agent
or a PM override).

## Consequences

- More ingestion code than a single embed-everything pipeline.
- Every citation in the UI can point at an exact row or page, not an approximate chunk.
- `evidence_level` becomes a meaningful, inspectable field instead of a constant.

See [`../architecture/03-ingestion.md`](../architecture/03-ingestion.md).
# 0002 — Gate every agent step, not just the drafted requirement and its score

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted, partly superseded by [0005](0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md) (the manual "Run" click per agent was removed; accepting a step now starts the next)

## Context

The first pass at this architecture gated the PM in at two points: after a requirement was
drafted, and after it was scored. Everything upstream of drafting — four-plus research agents
reading feedback, option data, sales data, and the web — ran fully unattended and handed the PM a
single combined result to review at the end.

That's cheap to build but expensive to use: if the PM disagrees with one finding from the
Competitor Agent, there's no way to fix just that without re-running (or manually untangling) the
whole batch. It also means a PM can't steer research mid-flight ("focus on EU hot-climate
feedback") — only after the fact.

## Decision

Model a run as an ordered/partially-ordered sequence of `Step`s, one per agent invocation. A step
only starts when the PM explicitly clicks "Run" on it (not automatically, even once its
dependencies are satisfied), and its output — always rendered as a short human-readable summary,
never just raw structured data — only unlocks the next step once the PM clicks **Accept**. **Edit**,
**Retry** (with a steering note), and **Reject** are available at every step, not just at the end.

See [`../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md).

## Consequences

- More PM clicks per run than a single end-of-pipeline review. Deliberate — the brief explicitly
  asks for the PM to be "firmly in control of every decision," not just the final one.
- Steering ("retry, but exclude X") becomes cheap and targeted instead of "reject everything, try
  again."
- The audit trail gains one entry per step action, not just one per finished requirement — more
  log volume, but it's what makes a run fully reconstructable after the fact (see
  [`../architecture/07-audit-trail.md`](../architecture/07-audit-trail.md)).
- Requires the orchestrator (LangGraph) to expose an `interrupt()` at every step boundary, not just
  two — informed the tech-stack choice, see
  [`../architecture/09-tech-stack.md`](../architecture/09-tech-stack.md).
# 0003 — Add a Critic Agent; split Competitor from Market/Trend

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

Original agent roster had one "Market & Competitor Agent" and relied entirely on `evidence_level`
grading plus the PM's own judgment to catch weak or unsupported claims. A reference architecture
sketch (layered component view, not authored in this repo) proposed two changes worth adopting.

## Decision

1. **Add a Critic Agent** that sits between every agent and the PM review queue: verifies every
   claim has a live citation, forces a retry on anything unsupported, and downgrades
   `evidence_level` on thin-but-technically-cited claims — *before* the PM ever sees the output.
2. **Split Competitor from Market/Trend** into two agents. Competitor findings are close to
   verifiable fact (a rival ships a feature or it doesn't); market/trend findings are inherently
   speculative (what will 2030 customers want). Keeping them separate keeps that evidence-character
   difference visible on each requirement's assumptions, instead of averaging it away inside one
   "market research" blob.

## Consequences

- One more agent in the roster, but it directly cheapens "push back on agent results" for the PM —
  obviously weak output is caught before it reaches a human.
- Assumptions/uncertainties on a requirement can now distinguish "this rests on a competitor fact"
  from "this rests on a trend guess."

See [`../architecture/01-agents.md`](../architecture/01-agents.md).
# 0004 — Supabase Postgres + pgvector for storage; OpenAI embeddings

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

The tech stack named "Postgres + pgvector" without choosing a host or an embedding model. A
Supabase project already exists, and an OpenAI API key is available in `.env`. Claude does not
produce embeddings, so a second provider is needed.

## Decision

1. **Host on Supabase.** One managed Postgres holds relational entities, embeddings (pgvector
   0.8), the LangGraph checkpointer state, and the docs mirror tables. Raw PDFs/Excel stay out of
   git (`data/` is gitignored); Supabase Storage can hold them later.
2. **Embed with OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`** (1536 dims, cosine distance, HNSW index). Only
   `finding.text` and `chunk.content` are embedded. Option codes and sales volumes stay exact,
   un-embedded data, joined and filtered directly.
3. **Backend-only access for now.** RLS is enabled on every table with no policies; only the
   service role or a direct connection can read/write. The frontend goes through the API.
4. **Append-only audit log enforced in the database** with triggers, not just application code.
5. **Schema is applied via migration files** committed under `supabase/migrations/`.

## Consequences

- The vector dimension is fixed in the column type. Switching model (e.g. `text-embedding-3-large`
  or Voyage) means re-embedding all rows and altering the column.
- LangGraph's Postgres checkpointer needs the direct or session-pooler connection string.
- Browser clients cannot query tables directly until RLS policies are added.
- 11 foreign keys are unindexed by choice (tables empty); revisit once query patterns are known.
- The feedback files' languages are not yet verified; if retrieval quality is poor on the real
  data, revisit the embedding model.

See [`../architecture/09-tech-stack.md`](../architecture/09-tech-stack.md) and
[`../architecture/04-data-model.md`](../architecture/04-data-model.md#as-implemented-supabase-supabasemigrations20261010_init_schemasql).
# 0005 — Chat entry point; orchestrator plans the agents; accept starts the next one

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Supersedes part of [0002](0002-stepwise-agent-approval-chain.md)

## Context

Decision 0002 gated every agent step, but kept all five research agents as visible cards that the
PM launched by hand, in any order, with a separate "Run" click per agent. In practice the PM wants
to ask a research question in natural language and have the system work out which agents are
needed, then review each agent's answer in turn.

## Decision

1. **Chat is the entry point.** A PM starts a new chat with a research request; each request
   creates a `PipelineRun` tied to that conversation.
2. **The orchestrator plans.** It selects the agents needed for the request, shows the plan with a
   reason per agent, and the PM can edit it before the first agent starts. The orchestrator may
   revise the remaining plan as results come in; changes are announced in the chat.
3. **Accept starts the next agent.** The separate manual "Run" click (the `awaiting_launch` state)
   is removed. Steps run strictly one at a time; the next needed agent starts when the previous one
   is accepted. This replaces the part of 0002 that said accepting only unlocks the next step.
4. **Push back in the chat.** Edit / Retry (steering note) / Reject remain available at every step;
   Retry is a reply on the step's thread.
5. **No final result before all needed agents are accepted.** Every claim in it carries a citation
   to a retrieved finding (source + locator).
6. **Not every agent runs every time.** Drafting, Prioritization, and Documentation are added only
   when the request asks for requirements.

## Consequences

- Fewer clicks than 0002 (one per step, not two), and the PM still reviews every agent output
  before the next one starts.
- The orchestrator is now a real planning component (an LLM call that chooses agents), not just a
  state machine. Its choices must be visible and overridable, which is why the plan is shown and
  editable.
- Step states become `planned → running → awaiting_review → accepted | rejected`. This needs a
  schema migration: `step.status` currently allows `queued` / `awaiting_launch`, and there are no
  `conversation` / `message` tables yet. **Pending — not yet applied.**
- LangGraph still maps well: one `interrupt()` per step, plus a planner node at the start.

See [`../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md).
# 0006 — Load Excel as raw relational tables; chunk PDFs per page with real citations

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

Opening the provided data changed two assumptions in the earlier docs:

- The "OptionList" PDFs are German sales catalogs (spec tables, equipment tables with ■/□ marks
  and prices, some prose), not clean option listings.
- The feedback spreadsheets carry far more structure than the `finding` table holds: country,
  engine type, feedback type, and a three-level category label. The customer-study workbook is a
  cross-tab, not a flat table, and the sales workbook is tiny.

## Decision

1. **Load every Excel file as raw rows first**, keeping the original columns plus sheet and
   row/cell: `feedback_raw` (comment embedded), `sales_volume`, `study_response`. `finding` rows
   are derived later by the agents and point back to these rows. Counts and filters run in SQL;
   only comments are searched by meaning.
2. **Chunk PDFs per page at headings** (≤ ~1,800 chars), store `page` + verbatim text, embed with
   OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`. A citation is always `file + page + quote` taken from the
   retrieved row, never generated by the model.
3. **Do not trust flattened equipment tables for variant availability.** The answer prompt tells the
   model to say a table needs checking rather than map ■/□ to a model. Table-aware extraction is
   deferred.
4. **Loaders live in `ingest/`**, are idempotent, and read `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (direct connection) and
   `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env`. They use autocommit so each transaction block really commits.
5. **Raw BMW files stay out of git** (`data/` is gitignored).

## Consequences

- Reuses the existing `Vfc` category labels as a candidate first level of the taxonomy.
- `G68` (Chinese 5 Series variant) appears in the studies and sales data (`G60_G68` sheet); the
  ontology must handle it.
- Study cells have no respondent counts, so they cannot carry a sample size.
- Open items: merge tiny PDF chunks, build the Tier 1 `option` extraction, derive `findings`,
  verify study values against the workbook, and migrate the pending chat tables (decision 0005).

# Competitor benchmarking: from one BMW to a comparable rival set > Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 [`01-agents.md`](01-agents.md) says the Competitor Agent "searches the web for competitor specs and reviews." That hides the hard part: *which* competitors, and how their evidence is made comparable to ours. This doc is a proposed processing structure for exactly that — start from one BMW (demo: 5 Series / G60), end with findings that say where rivals in the same bracket are ahead or behind *as customers experience it*. ## The six stages ```mermaid flowchart LR A["1 Anchor
fix one vehicle
→ VehicleProfile"] B["2 Segment definition
bands on price · range ·
seats · equipment"] G1{{"PM gate:
confirm bands"}} C["3 Long-list
load every model
inside the bands"] D["4 Shortlist
rank by similarity,
split by market"] G2{{"PM gate:
pick rivals"}} E["5 Evidence collection
specs · reviews ·
owner reports"] F["6 Relative comparison
per aspect, vs. the
anchor's own feedback"] G3{{"PM gate:
accept findings"}} A --> B --> G1 --> C --> D --> G2 --> E --> F --> G3 ``` ### 1 — Anchor: fix one vehicle "5 Series" is not one car: it spans combustion, plug-in and electric (i5), saloon and Touring, and a price range wide enough to overlap two segments. The PM picks a vehicle line **and** an anchor variant (or a small set of them); everything downstream is relative to that. Output is a `VehicleProfile` — the same structure later filled in for every rival: | Attribute | Example (illustrative) | Filled from | |---|---|---| | body style, seats | saloon, 5 | OptionList / official spec | | powertrain | BEV | official spec | | base price, typical transaction price | per market, in local currency | official price list | | range / consumption | WLTP (EU), EPA (US), CLTC (CN) | official spec | | dimensions, boot volume | length, wheelbase, litres | official spec | | equipment flags | standard vs. optional per feature | parsed `Options` table ([`03-ingestion.md`](03-ingestion.md)) | Every value carries a source locator, like any other `Finding`. ### 2 — Segment definition: what "the same bracket" means A `SegmentDefinition` is a set of criteria over `VehicleProfile` attributes, each either a **hard filter** (outside → excluded) or a **soft criterion** (only affects similarity ranking). | Criterion | Default derived from the anchor | Kind | |---|---|---| | Price | anchor base price −15 % … +25 % | hard | | Body style | same class (saloon/estate ↔ saloon/estate) | hard | | Seats | equal | hard | | Powertrain | same type | soft (hard if PM wants BEV-only) | | Range | ±20 % | soft | | Dimensions | length ±5 % | soft | | Equipment level | overlap of standard-equipment flags | soft | The percentages are placeholders to be calibrated, and the defaults are a proposal, not a rule: **the PM can override any band by hand** ("price 55–80 k €", "include PHEVs") before anything is searched. The chosen bands are stored with the run, so the rival set is reproducible and an auditor can see *why* a car was in or out. Price is used here only to draw the bracket. It never becomes a requirement — pricing stays out of scope per [`00-overview.md`](00-overview.md#scope). ### 3 — Long-list: load every model inside the bands Goal is recall, not precision: every model on sale in the target market that passes the hard filters. Two sources, merged and deduplicated on `(make, model, generation, variant)`: - **Structured catalogues first** — official manufacturer spec/price pages and public vehicle databases. `official` trust tier, deterministic parse where possible. - **Web search as a gap-filler** — "alternatives to …" / comparison-test articles surface rivals the catalogue pass missed (new entrants, China-only brands). Each candidate gets a `VehicleProfile`. Attributes that could not be sourced stay `null` and are shown as such — a missing range figure must not silently pass a range filter. ### 4 — Shortlist: pick the comparison vehicles Candidates are ranked by a similarity score (weighted distance over the soft criteria, weights visible and editable). The PM sees a table per market and ticks the rivals to carry forward — typically 3–6 per market. Markets are separate lists, not one global one: a rival that matters in China may not be sold in Europe at all. Result is a `CompetitorSet` per `(anchor, market)`. ### 5 — Evidence collection: scrape per shortlisted rival For each rival, the existing web ingestion path is reused (robots.txt respected, trust tier per domain from the domain config, unknown domains treated as the lowest tier): | Source type | Trust tier | Used for | |---|---|---| | Manufacturer spec / price pages | `official` | completing the `VehicleProfile` | | Comparison tests, long-term reviews | `trade_press` | expert judgement per aspect | | Owner reviews, forums | `forum_social` | customer experience — the counterpart to our own feedback data | Text is chunked, classified onto the same domain taxonomy as BMW's own feedback ([`08-scaling-and-config.md`](08-scaling-and-config.md)), and stored as `Finding`s tagged with the rival's `vehicle_id`. ### 6 — Relative comparison against the anchor This is where apples meet pears: BMW's side is internal survey data with known sample sizes, the rival's side is scraped public text. Putting raw numbers next to each other would be misleading. The comparison is therefore constrained on purpose: 1. **Compare per aspect, never per car.** Unit of comparison is one ontology domain or sub-topic ("rear legroom", "charging speed", "infotainment responsiveness"), not an overall verdict. 2. **Like with like.** Owner voice is compared with owner voice, expert tests with expert tests, spec with spec. For the anchor, the same public sources are scraped too — so the public-data comparison is BMW-public vs. rival-public, and the internal feedback is used to *confirm or contradict* it, not as the other side of the scale. 3. **Relative, not absolute.** Per aspect and source type: share of mentions and sentiment balance within that vehicle's own corpus. Cells with a clear delta become `Finding`s — `competitor_advantage` where the rival leads, and (proposed new signal type) `competitor_weakness` where BMW leads and the lead is worth defending. # 0001 — Two-tier PDF ingestion instead of naive text extraction

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

The provided PDFs (`*_OptionList.PDF`) are structured option/equipment listings. The brief asks
for findings and requirements that are traceable to their sources. A naive "dump the PDF to text,
chunk by token count, embed" pipeline would destroy the table structure and produce citations like
"chunk 47" instead of a page/row a PM could actually go look at.

## Decision

Parse every PDF (and, by extension, every source) on two tracks:

1. **Deterministic** — layout-aware table extraction into typed rows, no model in the loop. Feeds
   structured stores (e.g. an `Options` table) directly.
2. **Semantic** — heading-aware chunking + embedding for narrative text, locator kept per chunk.

Both converge on a `Finding` with a locator and an `evidence_level` set by *how* it was extracted
(`Verified` for deterministic, `Interpreted` for semantic — further gradable by the Critic Agent
or a PM override).

## Consequences

- More ingestion code than a single embed-everything pipeline.
- Every citation in the UI can point at an exact row or page, not an approximate chunk.
- `evidence_level` becomes a meaningful, inspectable field instead of a constant.

See [`../architecture/03-ingestion.md`](../architecture/03-ingestion.md).
# 0002 — Gate every agent step, not just the drafted requirement and its score

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted, partly superseded by [0005](0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md) (the manual "Run" click per agent was removed; accepting a step now starts the next)

## Context

The first pass at this architecture gated the PM in at two points: after a requirement was
drafted, and after it was scored. Everything upstream of drafting — four-plus research agents
reading feedback, option data, sales data, and the web — ran fully unattended and handed the PM a
single combined result to review at the end.

That's cheap to build but expensive to use: if the PM disagrees with one finding from the
Competitor Agent, there's no way to fix just that without re-running (or manually untangling) the
whole batch. It also means a PM can't steer research mid-flight ("focus on EU hot-climate
feedback") — only after the fact.

## Decision

Model a run as an ordered/partially-ordered sequence of `Step`s, one per agent invocation. A step
only starts when the PM explicitly clicks "Run" on it (not automatically, even once its
dependencies are satisfied), and its output — always rendered as a short human-readable summary,
never just raw structured data — only unlocks the next step once the PM clicks **Accept**. **Edit**,
**Retry** (with a steering note), and **Reject** are available at every step, not just at the end.

See [`../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md).

## Consequences

- More PM clicks per run than a single end-of-pipeline review. Deliberate — the brief explicitly
  asks for the PM to be "firmly in control of every decision," not just the final one.
- Steering ("retry, but exclude X") becomes cheap and targeted instead of "reject everything, try
  again."
- The audit trail gains one entry per step action, not just one per finished requirement — more
  log volume, but it's what makes a run fully reconstructable after the fact (see
  [`../architecture/07-audit-trail.md`](../architecture/07-audit-trail.md)).
- Requires the orchestrator (LangGraph) to expose an `interrupt()` at every step boundary, not just
  two — informed the tech-stack choice, see
  [`../architecture/09-tech-stack.md`](../architecture/09-tech-stack.md).
# 0003 — Add a Critic Agent; split Competitor from Market/Trend

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

Original agent roster had one "Market & Competitor Agent" and relied entirely on `evidence_level`
grading plus the PM's own judgment to catch weak or unsupported claims. A reference architecture
sketch (layered component view, not authored in this repo) proposed two changes worth adopting.

## Decision

1. **Add a Critic Agent** that sits between every agent and the PM review queue: verifies every
   claim has a live citation, forces a retry on anything unsupported, and downgrades
   `evidence_level` on thin-but-technically-cited claims — *before* the PM ever sees the output.
2. **Split Competitor from Market/Trend** into two agents. Competitor findings are close to
   verifiable fact (a rival ships a feature or it doesn't); market/trend findings are inherently
   speculative (what will 2030 customers want). Keeping them separate keeps that evidence-character
   difference visible on each requirement's assumptions, instead of averaging it away inside one
   "market research" blob.

## Consequences

- One more agent in the roster, but it directly cheapens "push back on agent results" for the PM —
  obviously weak output is caught before it reaches a human.
- Assumptions/uncertainties on a requirement can now distinguish "this rests on a competitor fact"
  from "this rests on a trend guess."

See [`../architecture/01-agents.md`](../architecture/01-agents.md).
# 0004 — Supabase Postgres + pgvector for storage; OpenAI embeddings

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

The tech stack named "Postgres + pgvector" without choosing a host or an embedding model. A
Supabase project already exists, and an OpenAI API key is available in `.env`. Claude does not
produce embeddings, so a second provider is needed.

## Decision

1. **Host on Supabase.** One managed Postgres holds relational entities, embeddings (pgvector
   0.8), the LangGraph checkpointer state, and the docs mirror tables. Raw PDFs/Excel stay out of
   git (`data/` is gitignored); Supabase Storage can hold them later.
2. **Embed with OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`** (1536 dims, cosine distance, HNSW index). Only
   `finding.text` and `chunk.content` are embedded. Option codes and sales volumes stay exact,
   un-embedded data, joined and filtered directly.
3. **Backend-only access for now.** RLS is enabled on every table with no policies; only the
   service role or a direct connection can read/write. The frontend goes through the API.
4. **Append-only audit log enforced in the database** with triggers, not just application code.
5. **Schema is applied via migration files** committed under `supabase/migrations/`.

## Consequences

- The vector dimension is fixed in the column type. Switching model (e.g. `text-embedding-3-large`
  or Voyage) means re-embedding all rows and altering the column.
- LangGraph's Postgres checkpointer needs the direct or session-pooler connection string.
- Browser clients cannot query tables directly until RLS policies are added.
- 11 foreign keys are unindexed by choice (tables empty); revisit once query patterns are known.
- The feedback files' languages are not yet verified; if retrieval quality is poor on the real
  data, revisit the embedding model.

See [`../architecture/09-tech-stack.md`](../architecture/09-tech-stack.md) and
[`../architecture/04-data-model.md`](../architecture/04-data-model.md#as-implemented-supabase-supabasemigrations20261010_init_schemasql).
# 0005 — Chat entry point; orchestrator plans the agents; accept starts the next one

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Supersedes part of [0002](0002-stepwise-agent-approval-chain.md)

## Context

Decision 0002 gated every agent step, but kept all five research agents as visible cards that the
PM launched by hand, in any order, with a separate "Run" click per agent. In practice the PM wants
to ask a research question in natural language and have the system work out which agents are
needed, then review each agent's answer in turn.

## Decision

1. **Chat is the entry point.** A PM starts a new chat with a research request; each request
   creates a `PipelineRun` tied to that conversation.
2. **The orchestrator plans.** It selects the agents needed for the request, shows the plan with a
   reason per agent, and the PM can edit it before the first agent starts. The orchestrator may
   revise the remaining plan as results come in; changes are announced in the chat.
3. **Accept starts the next agent.** The separate manual "Run" click (the `awaiting_launch` state)
   is removed. Steps run strictly one at a time; the next needed agent starts when the previous one
   is accepted. This replaces the part of 0002 that said accepting only unlocks the next step.
4. **Push back in the chat.** Edit / Retry (steering note) / Reject remain available at every step;
   Retry is a reply on the step's thread.
5. **No final result before all needed agents are accepted.** Every claim in it carries a citation
   to a retrieved finding (source + locator).
6. **Not every agent runs every time.** Drafting, Prioritization, and Documentation are added only
   when the request asks for requirements.

## Consequences

- Fewer clicks than 0002 (one per step, not two), and the PM still reviews every agent output
  before the next one starts.
- The orchestrator is now a real planning component (an LLM call that chooses agents), not just a
  state machine. Its choices must be visible and overridable, which is why the plan is shown and
  editable.
- Step states become `planned → running → awaiting_review → accepted | rejected`. This needs a
  schema migration: `step.status` currently allows `queued` / `awaiting_launch`, and there are no
  `conversation` / `message` tables yet. **Pending — not yet applied.**
- LangGraph still maps well: one `interrupt()` per step, plus a planner node at the start.

See [`../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](../architecture/02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md).
# 0006 — Load Excel as raw relational tables; chunk PDFs per page with real citations

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted

## Context

Opening the provided data changed two assumptions in the earlier docs:

- The "OptionList" PDFs are German sales catalogs (spec tables, equipment tables with ■/□ marks
  and prices, some prose), not clean option listings.
- The feedback spreadsheets carry far more structure than the `finding` table holds: country,
  engine type, feedback type, and a three-level category label. The customer-study workbook is a
  cross-tab, not a flat table, and the sales workbook is tiny.

## Decision

1. **Load every Excel file as raw rows first**, keeping the original columns plus sheet and
   row/cell: `feedback_raw` (comment embedded), `sales_volume`, `study_response`. `finding` rows
   are derived later by the agents and point back to these rows. Counts and filters run in SQL;
   only comments are searched by meaning.

   OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`. A citation is always `file + page + quote` taken from the
   retrieved row, never generated by the model.

   model to say a table needs checking rather than map ■/□ to a model. Table-aware extraction is

- Study cells have no respondent counts, so they cannot carry a sample size.
- Open items: merge tiny PDF chunks, build the Tier 1 `option` extraction, derive `findings`,
  verify study values against the workbook, and migrate the pending chat tables (decision 0005).

"""Extract text per page from the catalog PDFs and split it into citable chunks.

Every chunk keeps the file name, page number and its exact text, so an answer can quote the
real PDF. Needs `pdftotext` (poppler) on PATH.
"""
import re
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

MAX_CHARS = 1800
MIN_CHARS = 40
HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-ZÄÖÜ0-9][A-ZÄÖÜ0-9 &/,\-–\.\*]{5,70}$")


@dataclass
class Chunk:
    file: str
    title: str
    page: int
    index: int          # position of the chunk within the page
    heading: str | None
    text: str           # normalised page text, verbatim otherwise: this is the quotable citation

    @property
    def locator(self) -> str:
        return f"p.{self.page}"

    @property
    def embed_input(self) -> str:
        head = f"{self.title} — Seite {self.page}"
        if self.heading:
            head += f" — {self.heading}"
        return f"{head}\n{self.text}"


def _pdf_title(path: Path) -> str:
    out = subprocess.run(["pdfinfo", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("Title:"):
            return line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() or path.stem
    return path.stem


def _page_count(path: Path) -> int:
    out = subprocess.run(["pdfinfo", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return int(next(l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("Pages:")).split(":")[1])


def _page_lines(path: Path, page: int) -> list[str]:
    raw = subprocess.run(
        ["pdftotext", "-layout", "-f", str(page), "-l", str(page), str(path), "-"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout
    lines = [re.sub(r"[ \t­]+", " ", l).strip() for l in raw.splitlines()]
    return [l for l in lines if l]


def chunk_pdf(path: Path) -> list[Chunk]:
    title = _pdf_title(path)
    chunks: list[Chunk] = []
    for page in range(1, _page_count(path) + 1):
        lines = _page_lines(path, page)
        if sum(len(l) for l in lines) < MIN_CHARS:
            continue
        heading, buf, size, idx = None, [], 0, 0

        def flush():
            nonlocal buf, size, idx
            text = "\n".join(buf).strip()
            if len(text) >= MIN_CHARS:
                chunks.append(Chunk(path.name, title, page, idx, heading, text))
                idx += 1
            buf, size = [], 0

        for line in lines:
            if HEADING_RE.match(line) and len(line) > 5:
                flush()
                heading = line.rstrip(".")
            if size + len(line) > MAX_CHARS and buf:
                flush()
            buf.append(line)
            size += len(line) + 1
        flush()
    return chunks


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    for p in sys.argv[1:]:
        cs = chunk_pdf(Path(p))
        print(p, len(cs), "chunks; avg", sum(len(c.text) for c in cs) // max(len(cs), 1), "chars")

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import psycopg
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
from pdf_chunks import chunk_pdf  # noqa: E402

load_dotenv()
EMBED_MODEL = "text-embedding-3-small"
BATCH = 100


def vec(v: list[float]) -> str:
    return "[" + ",".join(f"{x:.7f}" for x in v) + "]"


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="chunk and embed, but do not write to the database")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    files = [Path(f) for f in args.files] or sorted(Path("data").glob("*_OptionList.PDF"))

    client = OpenAI()
    conn = None if args.dry_run else psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"])

    for path in files:
        vehicle_line = path.name.split("_")[0]
        chunks = chunk_pdf(path)
        embeddings: list[list[float]] = []
        for i in range(0, len(chunks), BATCH):
            batch = [c.embed_input for c in chunks[i:i + BATCH]]
            resp = client.embeddings.create(model=EMBED_MODEL, input=batch)
            embeddings += [d.embedding for d in resp.data]
        print(f"{path.name}: {len(chunks)} chunks embedded ({len(embeddings[0])} dims)")
        if conn is None:
            continue

        with conn.transaction():
            row = conn.execute("select id from public.source where uri = %s", (path.name,)).fetchone()
            if row:
                source_id = row[0]
                conn.execute("delete from public.chunk where source_id = %s", (source_id,))
            else:
                source_id = conn.execute(
                    "insert into public.source (type, uri, vehicle_line, title) values ('internal_pdf', %s, %s, %s) returning id",
                    (path.name, vehicle_line, chunks[0].title),
                ).fetchone()[0]

                conn.execute(
                    "insert into public.chunk (source_id, locator, heading, content, embedding, page, chunk_index) "
                    "values (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s::extensions.vector, %s, %s)",

    main()
"""Ask a question about the catalog PDFs and get an answer with real citations.

Usage:  python ingest/ask_pdf.py "Welche Felgen gibt es für den 5er?" [--line G60] [-k 8]
Needs OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_DB_URL in .env.
Citations are built from the retrieved chunks (file, page, verbatim text), never from model output.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re

import psycopg
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI

load_dotenv()
EMBED_MODEL = "text-embedding-3-small"
CHAT_MODEL = os.environ.get("OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini")

SYSTEM = (
    "You answer questions about BMW catalog PDFs using ONLY the numbered excerpts provided. "
    "Cite every statement with its excerpt number like [2]. If the excerpts do not contain the "
    "answer, say so plainly. Answer in the language of the question. The excerpts are flattened "
    "table text: a ■/□ mark cannot be reliably tied to a model column, so never state which model "
    "variant has an option as standard or optional; say that the table needs checking in the PDF."
)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("question")
    ap.add_argument("--line", help="restrict to a vehicle line, e.g. G60")
    ap.add_argument("-k", type=int, default=8)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    client = OpenAI()
    q = client.embeddings.create(model=EMBED_MODEL, input=args.question).data[0].embedding
    qv = "[" + ",".join(f"{x:.7f}" for x in q) + "]"
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"]) as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "select file, title, page, heading, content, similarity "
            "from public.match_chunks(%s::extensions.vector, %s, %s)",
            (qv, args.k, args.line),
        ).fetchall()
    if not rows:
        print("No chunks found. Have the PDFs been loaded?")
        return

    context = "\n\n".join(
        f"[{i}] {title}, Seite {page}" + (f", {heading}" if heading else "") + f"\n{content}"
        for i, (file, title, page, heading, content, _) in enumerate(rows, 1)
    )
    answer = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=CHAT_MODEL,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": f"Excerpts:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {args.question}"},
        ],
        temperature=0,
    ).choices[0].message.content
    print(answer, "\n")

    cited = sorted({int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", answer) if 1 <= int(n) <= len(rows)})
    print("Quellen / Sources:")
    for n in cited:
        file, title, page, heading, content, sim = rows[n - 1]
        quote = " ".join(content.split())[:300]
        print(f"[{n}] {file}, page {page}" + (f" ({heading})" if heading else "") + f"  [similarity {sim:.2f}]")
        print(f'    "{quote}"')


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
